name: Wyoming veterans: Veterans Commission service officers for claims help
description: Free help with VA disability and pension claims, health care and state and federal benefits from the Wyoming Veterans Commission’s veterans service officers. Call the statewide line to meet with the officer who covers your area.
next_step: Call the Wyoming Veterans Hotline, 1-800-833-5987, and ask to meet with a veterans service officer.
constraints: Service officers travel to outreach sites; call ahead to set a time.

name: Wyoming Aging Division and county senior centers
organization: Wyoming Department of Health, Aging Division, Community Living Section
description: The Aging Division funds senior centers in every county for supportive services, meals, caregiver support and Wyoming Home Services, and you apply through the senior center. Military service is not required.
next_step: Choose a county above for its senior centers, or call the Aging Division at 1-800-442-2766. Wyoming 2-1-1 also lists local services.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (Wyoming State Health Insurance Information Program)
organization: Wyoming Senior Citizens, Inc., Wyoming State Health Insurance Information Program (WSHIIP)
description: Free, one-on-one Medicare counseling from Wyoming’s State Health Insurance Information Program, Wyoming’s SHIP: Medicare, Medicare Savings Programs, prescription drug help and supplemental insurance.
next_step: Call WSHIIP toll-free at 1-800-856-4398. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Wyoming Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Wyoming Department of Health, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Department of Family Services, Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care settings, through three regional ombudsman offices. Adult Protective Services, in the Department of Family Services, takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults.
next_step: Choose a county above for its regional ombudsman, or call 1-800-856-4398. To report abuse, call your local Department of Family Services office (an on-call caseworker is available 24 hours a day), Adult Protective Services at 307-777-3602, or local law enforcement. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for older Wyoming residents
description: Legal Aid of Wyoming is funded by the Aging Division to provide supportive services for older adults, with offices in Cheyenne, Casper, Gillette and Lander.
next_step: Call the nearest Legal Aid of Wyoming office: Cheyenne 307-432-0808, Casper 307-232-9830, Gillette 307-459-5765, Lander 307-332-3517.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.

name: VA health care in Wyoming
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs: VA Cheyenne and VA Sheridan health care systems
description: Wyoming veterans are served by two VA health care systems: the Cheyenne VA Medical Center (2360 E. Pershing Blvd.; 307-778-7550, toll-free 888-483-9127) and the Sheridan VA Medical Center (1898 Fort Road; 307-672-3473), each with community clinics.
next_step: Call Cheyenne at 307-778-7550 or Sheridan at 307-672-3473 for appointments or VA Health Connect. Not enrolled yet? Ask a veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

name: Wyoming Independent Living
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 305 West First Street, Casper, WY 82601. Toll-free 800-735-8322.

name: Volunteers of America, Northern Rockies: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 20-ZZ-113): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 515-669-1780.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
